title: Route-aware quantization & batching + perishable-cache presets (draft)
content:
Summary:
This is a working draft of route-aware presets for batching, prefix/KV caching windows, and quantization profiles intended to be pluggable in the optimizer and surfaced as suggested defaults in the Console. Goal: provide concrete starting configs for common production routes so teams can quickly reduce unit cost while meeting latency SLOs, and also provide an example cost model snapshot for tradeoff evaluation.

Context and constraints (short):
- Many customers run heterogeneous endpoints: chat (low-latency interactive), high-throughput streaming chat, large-batch embeddings, and ad-hoc long-input summarization.
- The optimizer should pick presets by route metadata (SLO target, median input length, qps pattern).
- Conservative fallbacks: prefer slightly higher latency but better determinism if route declares strict SLOs.
- This is a pragmatic first pass — preserve easy toggles in Console: batch-size cap, cache-ttl, quant-profile override.

Presets (name, when to apply):
1) chat-interactive-low-latency
   - when: route SLO <= 150ms P90, typical input tokens <= 64, qps < 500 bursty
   - batch_size cap: 8 (auto-batcher target), burst coalescing = 20ms
   - max_batch_delay: 30ms
   - KV/prefix cache TTL: 3600s for identity tokens, 300s for ephemeral prefixes
   - quant_profile: q4_0 on GPU if validated for model; fallback q8_0 or fp16 if regen quality fails
   - routing: prefer low-latency pools (dedicated small-batch nodes)
   - expected unit cost tradeoff: ~20–40% token cost reduction vs baseline fp16 at minor latency increase

2) chat-high-throughput (streaming-friendly)
   - when: sustained qps > 400, typical inputs 8–48 tokens, latency SLO relaxed to 250–400ms
   - batch_size cap: 64 (allow autoscaler to open larger batch windows during steady state)
   - max_batch_delay: 120ms
   - KV/prefix cache TTL: 600s default (longer if high repetition observed)
   - quant_profile: q8_0 recommended for throughput-focused GPUs; q4_0 if model verified and quality checked
   - expected: 60–75% token cost reduction vs naive fp16 on same infra, tail latency can be controlled by max_batch_delay

3) embeddings-batch (offline/periodic)
   - when: large bulk jobs, non-interactive, input tokens per item vary (>=256)
   - batch_size cap: 128–512 depending on GPU memory and sequence length
   - max_batch_delay: 2000–5000ms allowed (job scheduler windows)
   - KV/prefix cache TTL: 0 (usually not helpful for embeddings)
   - quant_profile: q8_0 or int8 dynamic depending on libs; use model-specific calibration to avoid embedding drift
   - expected: maximize throughput; cost per vector down to low single-digit $/M tokens depending on GPU class

4) summarization-long-inputs
   - when: single requests with tokens >= 1024, SLO often relaxed (1–3s)
   - batch_size cap: 16–32 (to balance memory footprint and throughput)
   - max_batch_delay: 1500ms
   - KV/prefix cache TTL: 7200s for partial-prefix reuse (if clients reuse document ids)
   - quant_profile: q4_0 with fp16 fallback; if quant regression on ROUGE happens, raise to q8_0

5) low-traffic-ephemeral
   - when: qps < 5, unpredictable, sensitive to cold-starts
   - batch_size cap: 4
   - max_batch_delay: 60ms
   - KV/prefix cache TTL: 30–120s (perishable cache; short TTL prevents stale reuse across dissimilar requests)
   - quant_profile: default q8_0 (safer quality)

Perishable cache window rationale:
- 'Perishable' TTLs: short-lived caches (30–300s) for endpoints where semantics change quickly (ad-hoc completions, time-sensitive prompts). Allows a middle ground: capture immediate repetition without long-term semantic pollution.
- Longer TTLs (1–2 hours) for chat sessions where context re-use is very common.
- Metrics to collect: cache hit rate per route, latency delta for cache hit vs miss, semantic regression alerts (eval on small prompt set).

Quantization cascade idea (route-aware fallback):
- Default: q8_0 for safety. If model passes a small route-specific eval (100 prompts), enable q4_0.
- If a Q4-enabled route incurs >X% regression on quality metrics vs baseline fp16, automatically toggle to q8_0 and flag for PR review.
- Provide manual override in Console per-route and a bulk toggle for dedicated capacity pools.

Example cost-model snapshot (quick CSV paste to copy into spreadsheet):
Workload,Expected QPS,Typical Input Tokens,Batch Size,Max Delay ms,Cache TTL s,Quant Profile,Est Cost per 1M tokens (USD)
chat-low-latency,50,32,8,30,3600,q4_0,175
chat-high-throughput,800,24,64,120,600,q8_0,48
embeddings-batch,5,512,128,2000,0,q8_0,12
summarization-long,20,2048,16,1500,7200,q4_0,96
low-traffic-ephemeral,1,64,4,60,30,q8_0,240

Cost calc notes:
- Est Cost per 1M tokens is a quick back-of-envelope using our current runtime perf numbers (throughput per GPU, cost per-hour) — these will vary by region and GPU class.
- Use this CSV as an input to the detailed spreadsheet (we should map each preset to the existing cost model columns: gpu_type, tokens/s, effective_tokens_per_second_with_batching).

Operational concerns and metrics to report:
- Per-route: P50/P90 latency, cache hit ratio, batch size distribution, quant-profile in use, quality regression rate on eval suite.
- Global: fraction of traffic using q4_0 vs q8_0, cost savings delta month-over-month, incidents where fallback triggered due to quality regressions.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define X% threshold for auto rollback on quality regression (proposal: 3% metric delta on route eval or 5% user visible metric).
- Decide default per-GPU quant profile mapping (A100 vs L40 vs T4) — need microbenchmarks (see linked PR).
- Validate q4_0 for the top 10 models in catalog with route-specific prompt sets.
- Add a small UI flow in Console: "Preview cost and quality impact" when toggling quant_profile for a route.

Action items (owners):
- Marco: run per-model q4_0 vs q8_0 microbenchmarks (JIRA-INF-4321) — due 2026-03-20
- Dana: add telemetry hooks for cache TTL analytics and batch-size histogram — due 2026-03-15
- Aisha: wire the presets into optimizer suggestion APIs + wire sample CSV export — WIP

Notes to self / rough thinking: 
- Keep presets conservative but visible; teams should be able to opt-in to aggressive q4_0 via Console after seeing small eval.
- Preset naming: use stable keys (e.g., preset:chat.interactive.v1) so we can version-roll changes without breaking UI mappings.

References and links: 
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/OPTIMIZE-431 (optimize runbook and benchmark collection)
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 (batcher tuning flags)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-4321 (q4 validation tickets)

End of draft.

Unresolved: should we expose per-route 'max allowed quant downgrade' (boolean) so that for some routes we never allow q4_0? I think yes — add to next pass.
